entities.name: Developers
entities.rationale: Icon labeled DEVELOPERS at top center; developers push code to GitHub and consume results via UI/API on EC2. Not inside any container.

entities.name: GitHub
entities.rationale: GitHub logo labeled GITHUB at top left; external code repository that triggers events to Lambda and is cloned by Fargate. Not inside any container.

entities.name: Lambda
entities.rationale: Icon labeled LAMBDA (AWS_Icon_7); captures GitHub push events, triages and creates analysis requests. Standalone, no container.

entities.name: SQS
entities.rationale: Icon labeled SQS (AWS_Icon_6); queue for analysis requests, levels load and drives autoscaling. Standalone.

entities.name: ECS Fargate (Scanner)
entities.rationale: Icon labeled ECS FARGATE in the middle row (AWS_Icon_5); polls SQS, clones code from GitHub, analyzes it and pushes report to EC2. Standalone.

entities.name: EC2
entities.rationale: Icon labeled EC2 (AWS_Icon_4); receives analysis reports through an API, stores them in Aurora, and serves UI/API to users. Standalone.

entities.name: Aurora
entities.rationale: Icon labeled AURORA (AWS_Icon_1); database storing reports, used as temporary queue and final storage. Standalone.

entities.name: ECS Fargate (Compute Engine)
entities.rationale: Icon labeled ECS FARGATE at bottom right (AWS_Icon_2); Compute Engine that polls Aurora for reports, computes metrics, updates the database and writes to Elasticsearch. Standalone.

entities.name: ES
entities.rationale: Icon labeled ES (AWS_Icon_3); Elasticsearch storing optimized search data (in-house today, drawn with the Amazon Elasticsearch icon). Standalone.

visual_connections.description: Developers push code to the GitHub repo.
Curved arrow: code push triggers an event captured by Lambda.
Lambda creates an analysis request and places it on the SQS queue.
Arrow pointing from Fargate to SQS: the Fargate service polls the queue.
Diagonal arrow from Fargate up to GitHub: Fargate clones the code.
Fargate pushes the analysis report to the EC2 API.
Curved arrow from the left of EC2 down to Aurora: reports are stored in the database.
Two parallel arrows pointing from the Compute Engine to Aurora: polls the database to extract reports and updates it with computed results.
Short arrow up from the Compute Engine to ES: stores optimized search data.
Curved arrow from Developers down to EC2: users call the UI/API to view results.
